newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - May 13.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - May 13.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Tuesday morning:

** Communist coalition partners on Monday put pressure on the Janata Dal party of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral, asking its president to resign as chief minister of his state over a corruption scandal.

The scandal blew up last month after the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) said it planned to prosecute Laloo Prasad Yadav, chief minister of the eastern state of Bihar, and federal minister Chandradeo Prasad Varma.

"Instead of making it a partisan issue..., in the interest of parliamentary democracy, he (Yadav) must step down," Somnath Chatterjee, leader of the Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M), told the lower house, Lok Sabha.
** The Indian economy is shrugging off a worrisome slowdown that was reflected by dismal data released last week, and is on course for steady growth, analysts said on Monday.

They said a new tax-cutting budget and a more relaxed credit policy had set in motion a fresh wave of economic buoyancy that belied a sharp slowdown in exports, imports and industrial growth in the financial year ended March 31.

** The world's largest trading conglomerate, Japan's Mitsubishi Corporation has acquired one percent stake in the 25 billion-rupee Indian jeep and tractor major Mahindra & Mahindra Ltd, the Economic Times daily reports.
The paper says Mitsubishi's investment has a five-year lock-in period.
** The board of Maharashtra Glass & Agro Ltd has approved a hike in equity stake by French firm Sekurit Saint Gobain SAT, in the firm to 51 percent from 26 percent, the Financial Express says.
** Indian blue chips drifted lower on Monday, capping early gains as buyers stayed on the sidelines awaiting a possible oil price hike, dealers said.
Activity was concentrated in second-tier stocks, with increased investment buying seen in many software, bank and state-run firms, they said.
** Bombay's benchmark share index ended 34.09 points, or 0.90 percent, lower at 3,735.25.
** The National exchange index fell 12.85 points to 1040.50.
